slides.texte_overlay:
Habits of men who
are never bored
They always have a project going. A bike to restore, a song to learn, a trip to plan. Having something in progress gives every free evening a purpose instead of a scroll.
They say yes to small adventures. A new hiking trail, a concert of a band they don't know, a dinner at a cuisine they've never tried. Small risks keep life interesting.
They're curious about how things work. Bridges, engines, old buildings, why bread rises. Asking how something works turns ordinary days into a constant stream of discoveries.
They keep a list of things to try. Restaurants, books, places, skills. When a free Saturday comes, they never wonder what to do. They open the list and pick one.
They spend time with people older and younger than them. Grandparents, kids, colleagues of every age. Different generations bring stories you'll never hear from your friends.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Every day you discover something new, and boredom slowly stops being part of your life.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Every day brings something new, and boredom slowly disappears.

slides.texte_overlay: They move their body every day. A run, a swim, a walk without headphones. Physical energy turns into mental energy, and restless boredom has nowhere left to hide.
